title: Context ops cheat-sheet + reading notes (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose:
- Quick personal cheat-sheet for context/KV/cache/quantization ops that I can reference when debugging Private/Dedicated deployments or writing small experiment scripts. Not polished, just the memos I want saved.

High-level TL;DR I want to keep in head:
- KV/prefix caching gives ~2-6x effective throughput win on conversational workloads with high prefix reuse. Biggest wins when tokens-per-request is small relative to prefix length and when user sessions are sticky.
- Dynamic per-request batching + early-fill latency SLO policies reduce tail latency without huge throughput loss.
- Lower-bit quantization (4-bit) + small tuning on layernorm/softmax numerics helps most models with minimal quality loss, but per-model calibration still needed.

Papers/blogs skimmed (quick highlights):
1) "Efficient KV Caching for Long Contexts" (arXiv 2407.01234) - core bits: adaptive eviction using session-hit-rate; cost model ties memory pressure to price per-token. Notes: implement a cheap LRU+LFU hybrid with per-session TTL; measure hit-rate per model and surface to console as percentile.
2) "Latent Prefix Stashing" (blog post, internal link) - tradeoffs: precomputing prefixes useful for common system prompts; need to watch for personalization leaks if prefixes are shared across tenants. Suggestion: entropy-based prefix hashing to detect uniqueness.
3) "Practical 4-bit Quantization for LLM inference" - empirical: quantize weights but keep layernorm/softmax in fp16; calibrate scaling per-block. Notes: quantize then run 1-2 eval prompts and compute logprob delta; if > 0.6 bits/token drop back to 8-bit for that model.
4) "Batching strategies for tight SLOs" (conf talk notes) - early-fill buffers with priority queues (urgent=0ms latency SLO) + opportunistic backfilling for low-priority routes.
5) A few internal threads: "private-deploy memory footprint vs user retention" - ops: increase GPU memory margin by 10-15% for tails; enable prefix eviction for very long sessions.

Quick configuration heuristics (for Redwood Private / Dedicated):
- Default KV cache allocation per-GPU: 40% of device memory for 16GB GPUs, 30% for 32GB+, because larger devices give more headroom for kernels.
- Eviction policy: session-LRU with TTL 30m for consumer apps, 6h for enterprise interactive tools where sessions are persistent.
- Auto-batching window: 6ms for low-latency routes (<100ms SLO), 20-30ms for throughput-first.
- Quantization profile: try 4-bit with per-block outlier clipping threshold set to 2.5x; fallback to 8-bit if eval delta > 0.5 bits/token (config name: quant_profile:fast_infer_v2).

Experiment ideas to run (short tickets):
- EXP-ctx-01: Measure end-to-end latency/throughput with prefix cache enabled vs disabled on a microservice that has 70% reuse across first 16 tokens. Sweep cache TTL 5m/30m/2h. Logging: p95 hit-rate, p99 lat, cost-per-token.
- EXP-ctx-02: Try hybrid quantization: only quantize FFN layers and keep attention/query/proj in fp16. Evaluate perplexity and human eval on 200 prompts.
- EXP-ctx-03: Early-fill + priority queue for mixed SLOs: route queries labeled urgent/standard; measure impact on standard p95 and urgent p50.

Small command snippets I keep forgetting (pseudoconfig):
- enable prefix stash: true
- prefix_stash.eviction_policy: session_lru
- prefix_stash.max_size_mb: 8192
- batching.window_ms: 6
- batching.max_batch_tokens: 4096
- quant.profile: fast_infer_v2

Open questions / head-scratchers:
- How to safely share precomputed prefixes across tenants without leaking? Practical answer: per-tenant salt + varchar fingerprint of prompt; but still worry about accidental overlap with public system prompts. Maybe require consent for sharing cross-tenant prefix guts.
- Can we use a compact embedding to check prefix semantic-similarity and merge similar prefixes? Cost vs latency tradeoffs unclear.
- For very long context chains, is it better to evict oldest or compress to a summary and keep in cache? Need automated summary quality metric tied to downstream generation confidence.

Meeting notes (2025-01-28 sync with Mina/Harper):
- Mina: wants a cheap signal for when quantization is acceptable per model. Proposed metric: delta-nll on a 50-short-prompt probe. Action: make a small job that runs quantize->measure and writes calibration to model-metadata.
- Harper: asked about retailer use-case with many short chats. Suggested TTL 15m + aggressive batching window for scheduled bursts. Also flagged privacy review for prefix-sharing.
- Action items assigned: me (Zeke) to spin up EXP-ctx-01 and a small dashboard tile for "cache hit-rate by model/route".

Random heuristics / mental notes:
- If user churn high and prefix hit-rate low (<10%), turn off prefix caching for that route — caching overhead can hurt.
- When in doubt on quantization, prefer 8-bit for safety and only default to 4-bit in dedicated/reserved builds where we can control regression detection.
- Surface "cache eviction events" as traces in Redwood Console; they are small but tell you where sessions bleed memory.

Todo (personal):
- [ ] Create EXP-ctx-01 ticket + infra jenkins job (deadline: 2025-02-07)
- [ ] Prototype quant-probe runner and add to model onboarding flow
- [ ] Draft short RFC about safe prefix-sharing policy (privacy + engineering tradeoffs)
- [ ] Add cache-hit-rate panel to per-model dashboard (console)

Notes-to-self final lines:
- Keep list of small probes that are cheap to run on CI (100 prompts max). Make them idempotent and fast.
- When writing experimental results, include both absolute latency and cost-per-token numbers; engineering often focuses on latency but product needs cost.
- Ping SRE about increasing GPU memory slack for a subset of Private clusters for a 2-week trial.

--Zeke 2025-02-02
